findings.title: Reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
findings.description: A reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability was identified in the search functionality. Input provided by the user in the search parameter is not properly sanitized before being reflected in the response. This allows an attacker to inject arbitrary client-side scripts, which could lead to session hijacking, defacement, or redirection of users.
findings.recommendation: Implement proper input validation and output encoding for all user-supplied data, especially when reflecting it back to the client. Utilize a robust Web Application Firewall (WAF) and implement a Content Security Policy (CSP) to mitigate XSS attacks. Consider using client-side sanitization libraries and server-side strict encoding for all user inputs.

findings.title: Directory Traversal Vulnerability via /ftp Endpoint
findings.description: The `/ftp` endpoint on `juice-shop.herokuapp.com` is susceptible to directory traversal attacks. By manipulating the filename parameter with sequences like `../`, an attacker can access arbitrary files outside the intended directory. This could lead to the disclosure of sensitive server files such as configuration files, source code, or user data.
findings.recommendation: Implement strict input validation for all file-related parameters to prevent directory traversal sequences (e.g., `../`, `..\`). Ensure that file access is confined to a secure, sandboxed directory using absolute paths or chroot jails. Avoid directly concatenating user-supplied input with file paths.

findings.title: Missing CSP
findings.description: The Content-Security-Policy (CSP) header is not implemented on the server. CSP is a security standard that helps to prevent cross-site scripting (XSS), clickjacking, and other code injection attacks by specifying which dynamic resources (scripts, styles, images, etc.) are allowed to be loaded by the browser. Without CSP, a browser will load any resource, increasing the attack surface.
findings.recommendation: Implement a robust Content-Security-Policy header. Start with a strict policy that only allows resources from trusted sources (same-origin by default) and gradually relax it as needed, using directives like `script-src 'self'`, `style-src 'self'`, `img-src 'self' data:`, etc. Test the policy thoroughly in report-only mode (`Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only`) before enforcing it.

findings.title: SQLi
findings.description: SQLMap detected a time-based blind SQL injection vulnerability in the 'id' GET parameter. This allows an attacker to extract information from the database by observing delays in server responses based on injected SQL queries. The database management system was identified as PostgreSQL.
findings.recommendation: Implement parameterized queries or prepared statements to prevent SQL injection. Validate and sanitize all user input. Consider deploying a Web Application Firewall (WAF) to provide an additional layer of security. Ensure error messages do not disclose sensitive database information.

findings.title: Weak Authentication / Default Credentials Found
findings.description: The application was found to use weak authentication, specifically, default or easily guessable credentials for an administrative account. The credentials 'admin@juice-sh.op' and 'admin123' were successfully used to log in, indicating a severe security misconfiguration.
findings.recommendation: Implement strong password policies, enforce multi-factor authentication for all users, especially administrators. Disable default accounts or ensure their passwords are changed immediately upon deployment. Regularly audit user accounts and credential strength to prevent unauthorized access.
findings.poc: hydra -L /path/to/common_users.txt -P /path/to/common_passwords.txt juice-shop.herokuapp.com http-post-form "/rest/user/login:email=^USER^&password=^PASS^:F=Invalid email or password"

findings.title: TLS 1.0 Enabled
findings.description: TLS 1.0 is an outdated and insecure protocol. It is vulnerable to various attacks, including BEAST and POODLE. Its use is deprecated by security standards like PCI DSS, which requires disabling it.
findings.recommendation: Disable TLS 1.0 and TLS 1.1 on the server. Configure the server to support only TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3 to ensure strong encryption and compliance with modern security standards.

findings.title: Dev Subdomain Exposure
findings.description: A 'dev' subdomain was identified, potentially exposing development-specific configurations, unhardened services, or sensitive information not intended for public access. This could include debug interfaces, unprotected API endpoints, or source code repositories.
findings.recommendation: Review the contents of the 'dev' subdomain for sensitive data, misconfigurations, or exploitable services. Restrict access to internal networks or implement strong authentication. Consider removing or securing development environments once they are no longer needed.

findings.title: Potential Admin Interface Exposure
findings.description: An 'admin' subdomain was discovered, indicating a potential administrative interface. Such interfaces are often targets for credential stuffing, brute-force attacks, or privilege escalation attempts if not properly secured.
findings.recommendation: Verify if this subdomain hosts an administrative panel. Implement strong authentication policies (e.g., MFA), IP whitelisting, and rate limiting. Ensure all administrative functions are robustly protected against common web vulnerabilities.

findings.title: API Endpoint Exposure
findings.description: An 'api' subdomain was identified, suggesting the presence of a public-facing API. APIs can be vulnerable to a range of attacks including broken object-level authorization, excessive data exposure, injection flaws, and security misconfigurations.
findings.recommendation: Thoroughly audit the API endpoints for common API vulnerabilities (OWASP API Security Top 10). Implement robust authentication, authorization, input validation, and rate limiting. Ensure sensitive data is not unnecessarily exposed.

findings.title: CORS Wildcard
findings.description: The Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) policy for the endpoint '/api' is configured to allow requests from any origin, indicated by the 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *' header. This allows arbitrary third-party websites to make cross-origin requests to this endpoint, potentially leading to data leakage or unintended actions if sensitive information or state-changing operations are exposed without proper authentication and authorization checks. While some public APIs are designed this way, it can be problematic if the endpoint handles authenticated user data or sensitive operations.
findings.recommendation: Restrict the 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' header to a specific list of trusted domains rather than using a wildcard. If the API is truly public and intended for all origins, ensure that no sensitive data or actions requiring user authentication are exposed through this endpoint without robust server-side validation and authorization.

findings.title: S3 Bucket Publicly Accessible
findings.description: An S3 bucket named 'juice-shop-public-assets' is configured with public read access, allowing unauthenticated users to list and retrieve its contents. This could expose static assets, configuration files, or lead to information disclosure if sensitive data is stored here.
findings.recommendation: Restrict S3 bucket access to authenticated users only. Implement bucket policies and ACLs to enforce least privilege. Use S3 Block Public Access settings at the account or bucket level to prevent accidental public exposure.

findings.title: Security Group Allows All Ingress on Critical Ports
findings.description: A security group (sg-0abcdef1234567890) associated with a backend service (e.g., database, internal API server) allows unrestricted inbound traffic (0.0.0.0/0) on ports 3306 (MySQL) and 22 (SSH). This exposes internal services to the entire internet, significantly increasing the attack surface.
findings.recommendation: Restrict inbound traffic for critical ports to only trusted IP ranges or other security groups. For example, allow database access only from application server security groups. Close SSH port 22 or restrict it to specific administrative IPs/VPN ranges.

findings.title: IAM Role with Excessive Permissions
findings.description: The IAM role 'JuiceShopAppRole', likely assigned to the Heroku application's underlying AWS resources, has 'AdministratorAccess' or similar broad permissions (e.g., 's3:*', 'ec2:*', 'rds:*'). This violates the principle of least privilege and could be exploited if the application or a component using this role is compromised.
findings.recommendation: Review and revise the IAM policy attached to 'JuiceShopAppRole' to grant only the minimum necessary permissions required for the application's functionality. Implement custom policies instead of managed policies like 'AdministratorAccess' or 'PowerUserAccess'.
findings.poc: aws iam list-attached-role-policies --role-name JuiceShopAppRole; aws iam list-role-policies --role-name JuiceShopAppRole

findings.title: S3 Bucket Without Default Encryption
findings.description: The S3 bucket 'juice-shop-logs-backups', potentially storing application logs, backups, or other sensitive operational data, does not have default encryption enabled. While public access might not be an issue, data at rest is not encrypted, which could be a compliance or data privacy concern if the bucket is compromised.
findings.recommendation: Enable default encryption for the S3 bucket using S3-managed keys (SSE-S3) or AWS Key Management Service (KMS) keys (SSE-KMS) to protect data at rest.
findings.poc: aws s3api get-bucket-encryption --bucket juice-shop-logs-backups 2>&1 | grep -q 'ServerSideEncryptionConfigurationNotFoundError' && echo 'Bucket not encrypted' || echo 'Bucket encrypted'

findings.title: GCP Cloud Storage Bucket Publicly Accessible
findings.description: A Google Cloud Storage bucket named 'juice-shop-gcp-cdn-cache', potentially used for CDN caching or static content, is configured with 'allUsers' having read access. This exposes its contents to the entire internet, potentially revealing sensitive static assets, configuration files, or other data.
findings.recommendation: Remove the 'allUsers' or 'allAuthenticatedUsers' entry from the bucket's IAM policy. Restrict access to specific service accounts or users as needed, adhering to the principle of least privilege. If public access is intended for static content, ensure no sensitive data is present.

findings.title: K8s Dashboard Exposed
findings.description: The Kubernetes Dashboard, a web-based UI for managing Kubernetes clusters, is exposed to the public internet. This exposure allows unauthorized access to sensitive cluster information, including deployment details, pod logs, and potentially direct control over resources if authentication is misconfigured or bypassed. This is a critical security risk as it can lead to full cluster compromise.
findings.recommendation: It is strongly recommended to restrict access to the Kubernetes Dashboard. Do not expose the K8s Dashboard directly to the public internet. Implement strong authentication methods (e.g., OIDC, SAML) and role-based access control (RBAC) to limit user permissions. Access the dashboard only through a secure bastion host, VPN, or an authenticated proxy. Consider removing the Kubernetes Dashboard entirely if not strictly necessary, or replacing it with more secure alternatives for cluster management.

findings.title: BOLA / IDOR
findings.description: The application allows an unauthenticated or low-privileged user to retrieve sensitive information of other users by manipulating the `id` parameter in the `/api/v1/users/{id}` endpoint. For example, by changing the ID from their own user ID to `1` (which often corresponds to an administrator or another user), an attacker can access details like email, username, and potentially other profile information without proper authorization. This vulnerability indicates a Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA) or Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) flaw.
findings.recommendation: Implement robust authorization checks at the API endpoint `/api/v1/users/{id}` to ensure that a user can only access their own profile information or that of users they are explicitly authorized to view. All requests to access user data should be validated against the authenticated user's privileges on the server-side. Avoid relying solely on client-side authorization. Consider using UUIDs instead of sequential IDs to make enumeration harder, though this is not a primary defense against IDOR.

findings.title: AWS Key Leak
findings.description: An AWS Access Key ID and Secret Access Key were found exposed on the server, likely within an accessible `.env` configuration file. These credentials grant programmatic access to AWS resources associated with the account. Attackers can use these keys to access, modify, or delete data, launch instances, and incur charges, potentially leading to significant data breaches, service disruptions, and financial costs.
findings.recommendation: Immediately revoke the exposed AWS Access Key ID and Secret Access Key from the AWS IAM console. Review server configuration to ensure that sensitive files like `.env` are not publicly accessible (e.g., configure web servers to deny access, use environment variables for secrets, or secure infrastructure-as-code). Implement secrets management solutions (e.g., AWS Secrets Manager, HashiCorp Vault) and enforce least privilege principles for all credentials.

findings.title: Cloudflare WAF Detected
findings.description: The target application, juice-shop.herokuapp.com, is protected by Cloudflare's Web Application Firewall (WAF). Cloudflare provides a suite of services including DDoS mitigation, content delivery network (CDN), and a WAF to protect web applications from various cyber threats like SQL injection, cross-site scripting (XSS), and other OWASP Top 10 vulnerabilities. While Cloudflare enhances security, it's important to note that WAFs are not infallible and can sometimes be bypassed. Detection of a WAF indicates an active defense mechanism is in place.
findings.recommendation: For attackers: Attempt to identify specific Cloudflare WAF rules and look for known bypass techniques for the detected WAF version. Focus on client-side vulnerabilities or logic flaws that might not be fully mitigated by the WAF. For defenders: Ensure Cloudflare WAF rules are properly configured and updated regularly. Supplement WAF protection with robust input validation, secure coding practices, and regular security testing of the application itself.

findings.title: Weak/Default Administrator Credentials
findings.description: The application allows login with default, guessable administrator credentials (admin@juice-sh.op:admin123). This provides full administrative access to the application, allowing modification of content, user management, and access to sensitive data, leading to complete compromise of the application.
findings.recommendation: Immediately change default administrator credentials to a strong, unique password. Implement robust password policies (complexity, length, rotation), multifactor authentication, and account lockout mechanisms after a few failed login attempts. Regularly audit user accounts for weak or default passwords.

findings.title: Subdomain Takeover
findings.description: A subdomain takeover vulnerability was identified for 'shop.juice-shop.herokuapp.com'. The DNS record (CNAME) for this subdomain points to an external Heroku service ('juice-shop-old-app-1234.herokuapp.com') that appears to be unprovisioned or available for registration. An attacker could potentially register this abandoned Heroku application, gaining control over the subdomain 'shop.juice-shop.herokuapp.com'. This could lead to various attacks, including hosting malicious content, phishing, or bypassing security controls like CORS policies.
findings.recommendation: To remediate this vulnerability, immediately remove the dangling CNAME record for 'shop.juice-shop.herokuapp.com' from your DNS configuration. If the subdomain is intended for use, ensure that the corresponding Heroku application is properly provisioned, configured, and actively managed. If the subdomain is no longer needed, deleting the DNS record is the most effective way to prevent future takeovers.

findings.description: The response from https://juice-shop.herokuapp.com is missing the 'Strict-Transport-Security' security header.
findings.recommendation: Add the 'Strict-Transport-Security' header to all server responses.
